words.gloss: one — the singular noun already says this; وَاحِد just adds emphasis
two books — the dual ending alone says "two", no separate number word needed
three (feminine-form number, counting a masculine noun — the reversal rule for later)
the man (subject, following the verb — VSO order)
read (I) — the 1st-person past-tense ending, no gender marking
big (خبر كان, accusative — not the nominative ٌ a nominal sentence would use)
was (feminine — a helping kasra appears before الـ)
door (of — مُضَاف, no الـ or tanwīn of its own)
the house (مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ — genitive, carries the phrase's definiteness)
house (of — مُضَاف, here the nominative topic of the sentence)
go (you, m.) — the same تَـ prefix-form as "she goes"; only the pronoun tells them apart
go (you, f.) — تَـ plus the feminine ـِينَ ending
eleven (feminine — a different word from the masculine, not just a changed ending)
fifteen — خَمْسَةَ keeps the reversed agreement already known from 3-10, عَشَرَ agrees normally (masculine)
fifteen, feminine — both halves flip from the masculine: خَمْسَ loses its ة, عَشْرَةَ gains one
twenty — invariant, the same form for a masculine or feminine noun
twenty-one — ones-digit وَ tens; وَاحِدٌ agrees normally with the noun, exactly as it would alone
hundred (مُضَاف — governs a genitive noun, like an iḍāfa)
the one (feminine cardinal — one o'clock is the exception, not an ordinal)
the second (ordinal, agreeing with the hour)
the twelfth — an ordinal teen-compound, fixed on ـَ regardless of case, same as the cardinal teens
and the quarter — "past" uses وَ, same as the half
minus a quarter — "to" uses إِلَّا, not وَ

translit: awwalan, ishtarā aṭ-ṭālibu tadhkiratan. thumma sāfara bi-al-qiṭāri ilā al-madīnati. athnāʾa ar-riḥlati, qaraʾa kitāban. akhīran, waṣala al-qiṭāru, wa-rajaʿa aṭ-ṭālibu ilā al-bayti. kāna saʿīdan.
en: First, the student bought a ticket. Then he traveled by train to the city. During the trip, he read a book. Finally, the train arrived, and the student returned home. He was happy.
